issues.description: The template's dd_create_zero_state is annotated (and its docstring describes) returning a DDNode, while the problem statement and the solution expect/implement dd_create_zero_state to return a DD representing the full n-qubit zero state. This mismatch in the declared return type and description in the template can confuse students about what to construct and return and is inconsistent with the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template signature and docstring for dd_create_zero_state to match the specification and solution: annotate the return type as DD (-> DD), and adjust the docstring to state it returns a DD representing the n-qubit |0...0> state. This will align the template with the problem statement and the solution and avoid student confusion.

issues.description: The template's dd_create_zero_state function signature is annotated to return a DDNode, while the solution implementation (and the problem description) treat the returned object as a DD. This mismatched identifier for the same conceptual entity (the decision-diagram object representing the multi-qubit zero state) can confuse students about whether to construct/return a DD or a DDNode and where to use make_dd / terminal DDs.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template signature and documentation with the intended conceptual type by changing the template's dd_create_zero_state return annotation from DDNode to DD and clarifying the docstring to explicitly state it returns a DD (use the DD wrapper around DDNode with an edge weight). This matches the solution and the usage elsewhere in the exercise.
